speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start from the beginning: Can you describe exactly how your gait and balance problems have developed over time, and do you notice any specific patterns or triggers?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunken" appearance and right-sided clumsiness sound like ataxia; have you experienced any weakness, numbness, or loss of coordination in your hands or feet, and did these symptoms start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST TEST: Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) analysis including Oligoclonal bands and cell count.

Given your history with Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I need to rule out PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) or MS-related relapses immediately. Can you tell me if you have any new visual disturbances like blurred vision or "shimmering" spots, or any changes in your speech?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain - Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML); T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) analysis - Data not available.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
